faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

faqs.question: I see the message Communication Error when I use a USB connection. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Delete all print jobs in the print queue.
Turn the printer off.
Note:
Make sure the USB cable is connected correctly.
Restart your computer. When the desktop appears, turn your printer on and follow the on-screen instructions.
Note:
If the problem continues, turn the printer off again and delete the printer in the list of printers. Then disconnect the USB cable from the printer and connect it again.

faqs.question: What size ink packs are available?
faqs.answer:
The ink packs are available only in the 1-liter size.
Related references
Consumables and Replacement Parts

faqs.question: Can I use my product while the ink tanks are not installed?
faqs.answer:
No. The ink tanks must be installed for the printer to operate properly. Epson recommends the use of genuine Epson ink packs with the ink tanks.
Caution:
Epson cannot guarantee the quality or reliability of non-genuine Epson ink. The use of non-genuine ink may cause damage that is not covered by Epson's warranties, and under certain circumstances, may cause erratic printer behavior.

faqs.question: Can I use my product's ink packs and ink tanks with other Epson products?
faqs.answer: You can use them with the SureColor F6200, SureColor F7200, and SureColor F9200 but not with other Epson printers.

faqs.question: What is High-Density black ink?
faqs.answer:
High-Density black ink provides a bolder, richer black on your printed media than regular black ink. The High-Density black ink in the ink tank should be stirred once a week to prevent sedimentation and incorrect colors in your printed media. See the link below.
Related tasks
Stirring High Density Black Ink

faqs.question: What is the capacity of the ink tanks?
faqs.answer: The capacity of each tank is 1.5 liters.

faqs.question: Are other types of black ink available for my product?
faqs.answer:
No. Only High-Density black ink is available.
Caution:
Epson cannot guarantee the quality or reliability of non-genuine Epson ink. The use of non-genuine ink may cause damage that is not covered by Epson's warranties, and under certain circumstances, may cause erratic printer behavior.

faqs.question: How do I refill the ink tanks?
faqs.answer:
You need to replace the ink chip unit whenever you refill the ink tanks. Also check the ink levels and the message displayed on your control panel before refilling the ink tanks. The message and the current ink levels help to determine whether you need to refill the ink tanks or replace them. See the link below.
Related tasks
Replacing the Chip Unit and Refilling Ink

faqs.question: When should I replace the ink tank?
faqs.answer:
When the message
Refill Ink Tank
is displayed on the control panel screen and the remaining ink level is greater than 2.8 inches (70 mm) from the base of the ink tank, it is time to replace the ink tank. The ink tank must be replaced because fine dirt, dust, and other foreign material causes the ink tank’s filter to malfunction. The ink tank replacement interval depends on the usage environment and conditions. Contact Epson support for information on replacing components.

faqs.question: How many ink tanks are in my product?
faqs.answer: The printer has eight ink tanks: cyan (2), magenta (2), yellow (2), and High-Density black (2).

faqs.question: Can I wait to refill the ink tanks until they are completely empty?
faqs.answer:
No. The ink level must remain above 2.8 inches (70 mm) from the base of the ink tank at all times. If the ink level falls below 2.8 inches (70 mm), replace the ink chip unit and refill the ink as soon as possible. Failing to do so may allow air into the ink system and affect your printouts.
Related tasks
Replacing the Chip Unit and Refilling Ink

faqs.question: Do I need to install a new chip unit each time I refill the ink tank with a new ink pack?
faqs.answer: Yes, a new ink chip unit needs to be installed with every new ink pack. The chip is there to alert you when ink is low.

faqs.question: What is the capacity of the waste ink bottle?
faqs.answer: The bottle's capacity is 2 liters.

faqs.question: Can I reuse the chip unit that's on an ink pack?
faqs.answer: No, ink chip units are not reusable. A new chip unit is included with each new ink pack.

faqs.question: Can I use my product when the waste ink bottle is not installed?
faqs.answer:
No. The waste ink bottle must be installed at all times to catch ink that may leak out of the waste ink tubes. Make sure the waste ink bottle is installed even when the printer is not on.
Related tasks
Replacing the Waste Ink Bottle

faqs.question: How should I dispose the waste ink?
faqs.answer:
Leave the waste ink in the waste ink bottle and do not transfer it to another container. Check your local regulations and contact a local disposal service, if needed.
Related tasks
Replacing the Waste Ink Bottle

faqs.question: How often should I clean the platen, pressure rollers, and media holding plates?
faqs.answer:
Clean them as needed or when ink smears or drips onto your printed media. Clean them to remove ink, paper particles, and lint.
Caution:
If ink remains on these parts, it could transfer to your printouts. Continued use of your product with ink, paper particles, or lint on these surfaces could damage the print heads or clog the nozzles.
Related tasks
Cleaning the Platen, Pressure Rollers, and Media Holding Plates

faqs.question: How often should I stir the High-Density black ink in the ink tank?
faqs.answer:
To prevent sedimentation and incorrect colors in your printed media, stir the High Density Black ink in the ink tank once a week.
Open the ink inlet cover for the High Density Black ink shown here.
Grasp the loop at the top of the ink inlet cap and slowly remove the ink inlet cap.
Move the stirring stick up and down 15 times. Insert the stick completely into the ink tank and raise the stick up to the top each time.
Caution:
Move the stick slowly and steadily, or ink may splatter.
Insert the stirring stick into the ink tank and replace the ink inlet cap
Caution:
Press the ink inlet cap down firmly. If the slider comes into contact with the ink inlet cap when pulling it out, the cap could get damaged.
Close the ink inlet cover.

faqs.question: How often should I perform print head maintenance?
faqs.answer:
Perform print head maintenance as needed or when ink smears or drips onto your printed media even after you've cleaned the print heads. Also perform print head maintenance when the colors in your printout are faint or missing even after you've cleaned the print heads.
Related tasks
Checking for Clogged Print Head Nozzles
Cleaning the Print Head
Cleaning Around the Print Heads

faqs.question: Which media does my product support?
faqs.answer:
The printer prints on dye sublimation transfer paper. For media specifications, see below.
Media Specifications
Print quality is greatly affected by the type and quality of media used. Always test a sample of media before purchasing large quantities or printing large jobs.
Note:
Do not use media that is wrinkled, scratched, torn, or dirty.
Roll core size
2 or 3 inches
Roll outer diameter
Up to 9.8 inches (250 mm)
Media width
12 to 64 inches (300 to 1626 mm)
Media thickness
Up to 0.04 inch (1 mm)
Roll weight
Up to 88.2 lb (40 kg)

faqs.question: Which media does Epson recommend?
faqs.answer: Epson does not have any recommendations for media. You may need to try media from various manufacturers to find the most appropriate media for your use.

faqs.question: Can I sublimate to 100% cotton or a cotton/polyester blend?
faqs.answer: Yes, but Epson recommends sublimating to 100% polyester to achieve the best results. Epson cannot guarantee quality or color accuracy when sublimating to 100% cotton or cotton/polyester blends.

faqs.question: Which media width does my product support?
faqs.answer:
The printer supports a media width of 12 to 64 inches (300 to 1626 mm).
Related references
Media Specifications

faqs.question: Can I buy media for my product from Epson?
faqs.answer:
Yes, Epson offers media for this printer. However, most media is available through third-party vendors.
Related references
Media Specifications

faqs.question: Can I set the date and time on my product?

Important:
Contact the reseller for product installation. The product must be installed by an Epson authorized reseller. Damage to the product from unauthorized installation will not be covered by your Epson warranty.

faqs.question: Which interfaces does my product support?
faqs.answer:
Hi-Speed USB (compatible with the USB 2.0 specification) and 100BASE-T/1000Base-TX are supported.
Note:
Use a category 5 or better shielded twisted pair cable.

faqs.question: Does my product come with an Epson printer driver?
faqs.answer:
No, there is no standard Epson printer driver for the printer. Wasatch RIP software is used to print.
Note:
There is a Communication Driver (available for download) which is used to update the firmware.

faqs.question: Which software comes with my product?
faqs.answer:
The software below is included with the printer and is available for download from the printer's Downloads tab.
Epson Communication Driver for Windows
Epson LFP Remote Panel 2 Utility
EpsonNet Config Utility
EpsonNet Setup
EpsonNet Print
The Wasatch RIP software is also included, but it is not available from the Downloads tab for your product.

faqs.question: Where can I get the Communication Driver, utilities, or the firmware software for my product?
faqs.answer: You can download them from the Downloads tab for your product.
